usageNotes: Use this to discover which custom CPU model definitions are available cluster-wide before assigning a 'custom-*' cputype to a VM. Results are visibility-filtered by the caller's permissions on '/mapping/cpu/<name>', so an unprivileged token may see fewer entries than a root-equivalent user. Custom CPU model names are always prefixed with 'custom-' (e.g. 'custom-secure-baseline'); if no custom models have been defined the response will be an empty array.

examples.summary: List all custom CPU models visible to the current API token

tips: The 'digest' field in each returned entry can be passed to update/delete operations to prevent concurrent modification races.
The 'reported-model' field controls what the guest OS sees (e.g. 'Skylake-Server'), while 'cputype' is the internal Proxmox reference name; they are independent.
If the list is unexpectedly empty, verify the API token has at least 'Mapping.Audit' on '/mapping/cpu/' — without it, no entries will be returned even if models exist.
Setting 'hidden: true' on a custom model suppresses the KVM hypervisor signature, which can help with anti-VM software in Windows guests.
